summary: Describes a TLS extension for padding ClientHello messages to a desired size.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7685 lets a TLS client add zero bytes to its ClientHello so the message avoids sizes that trigger known implementation bugs. The server does not echo the padding extension.

questions: what is the tls padding extension
can a tls server echo the padding extension
why does tls pad the clienthello
subtitle: A TLS extension that pads ClientHello messages to avoid size-related implementation bugs.

tldr.problem: Some TLS implementations have bugs triggered by ClientHello messages of particular sizes, and patching every affected implementation may be difficult.
tldr.mechanism: A client can add a padding extension filled with zero bytes to make the ClientHello reach a desired size.
tldr.outcome: The server must not echo the extension; the RFC requires zero padding data to limit its use as a covert channel.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 7685's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC updates RFC 5246 with a TLS ClientHello padding extension.

sections.title: Why Pad a ClientHello
sections.content:
As TLS versions and extensions accumulated, ClientHello messages grew. The RFC says some implementation bugs were triggered by particular ClientHello sizes, and that making a message larger can avoid at least one such bug.

The extension gives a client a way to pad ClientHello to a chosen size without requiring every affected implementation to be patched first.
sections.plainLanguage: A TLS client can add padding to avoid message sizes that cause some servers to fail. The option works around the size-sensitive bug by changing the message length.

sections.title: The Padding Extension Data
sections.content:
The padding extension has type 21, and its extension data is any number of zero bytes. The data can be empty, but if present the client must fill it completely with zeros.

The server must not echo the extension. A client can calculate whether its ClientHello falls in a problematic size range and add enough padding to move beyond that range.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension contains zero bytes and can be empty. The client chooses the amount of padding; the server does not return it.

sections.title: Padding and Covert Channels
sections.content:
The RFC notes that arbitrary padding contents could carry hidden data. Requiring all padding bytes to be zero prevents that use of the contents, though the extension length can still carry a much smaller covert signal.

The extension is for adjusting the ClientHello size; it does not change the rest of the TLS handshake.
sections.plainLanguage: Zero-only padding prevents the data bytes from carrying hidden messages. The chosen padding length can still reveal a small amount of information.
